Context/Background: Immune checkpoint inhibitor therapy (ICI)-induced myositis (irMyositis) occurs in about 1% of patients treated with anti-PD1 or anti-CTLA-4 antibodies and can be debilitating or even fatal. We compared gene expression profiles from skeletal muscle biopsies between irMyositis patients, patients with spontaneous dermatomyositis (DM, comprising anti-Mi2-positive and anti-TIF1-γ-positive subtypes), and non-diseased controls (NDC). We used the NanoString nCounter PanCancer Immune Profiling Panel to perform differential gene expression (DGE) and pathway enrichment analyses.

Then, discuss the results, highlighting any differences seen in active immunological pathways.  Focus on differences betwen irMyositis and DM.

Introduction/Context  
Immune checkpoint inhibitor-induced myositis (irMyositis) and dermatomyositis (DM) were profiled by NanoString nCounter on skeletal muscle biopsies. Differential expression (DE) was performed for five contrasts: irMyositis vs Mi2-positive DM, irMyositis vs TIF1γ-positive DM, irMyositis vs non-diseased controls (NDC), Mi2-DM vs NDC, and TIF1γ-DM vs NDC. Raw counts and DE statistics (logFC, adj.P.Val) were provided; platform details, sample sizes, and replicates are not specified. We ran preranked GSEA using the Reactome_Pathways_2024 library on each DE gene list (ranked by logFC).

Keywords  
interferon signaling; antigen presentation; costimulation (CD28 family); TLR4 cascade; MHC class I

Candidate Genes  
MX1; ISG15; STAT1; CTLA4; PDCD1

Pathway Enrichments (Reactome_Pathways_2024)

1. irMyositis vs Mi2 (DM)

4. Mi2 (DM) vs NDC

| Cellular Responses to Stimuli | Up   | NFKBIA, MAPK1, VEGFA, NLRP3        |  
| Post-translational Modification | Up | PSMB8, TNFAIP3, IKBKG             |

5. TIF1γ (DM) vs NDC

|-------------------------------|-----------|--------------------------------|  
| Interferon Signaling          | Up        | ISG15, MX1, STAT1, OAS3       |  
| Interferon Alpha Beta Signaling | Up      | MX1, ISG15, IFIT1, OAS3       |  
| Cellular Responses to Stimuli | Up        | NFKBIA, MAPK1, NLRP3          |  
| Antigen Processing – Cross Presentation | Up | TAP1, HLA-A, HLA-B          |  
| Toll-Like Receptor 4 Cascade  | Up        | TLR4, IKBKB, MAPK3            |  

Analysis  
Across both DM subtypes (Mi2 and TIF1γ vs NDC), there is a near-universal upregulation of interferon signaling, antigen processing, TLR cascades and post-translational modification pathways (≈98% of enriched Reactome terms up), reflecting a classic type I/II IFN–driven myositis signature in DM versus controls. In contrast, irMyositis versus DM shows a flipped pattern: interferon-related and antiviral innate pathways are predominantly down in irMyositis (74–79% of enriched terms), while T-cell co-stimulatory modules (Adaptive Immune System; CD28 family) are relatively up. Compared to controls, irMyositis still exhibits strong interferon and antigen presentation upregulation (100% up), but when normalized to the already high baseline in DM, irMyositis shows a relative suppression of IFN-driven innate immunity and a relative enhancement of adaptive co-stimulation. This suggests that irMyositis may involve a shift from a dominant IFN signature toward checkpoint-responsive T-cell co-stimulation, in line with anti-PD1/CTLA-4 therapy mechanisms.

Differences Between irMyositis and DM  
– Interferon pathways (Alpha/Beta and Gamma) and antiviral ISG modules: strongly up in DM versus NDC, but down in irMyositis versus both Mi2 and TIF1γ.  
– Adaptive Immune System and Costimulation by CD28 family: uniquely enriched up in irMyositis versus DM, indicating heightened T-cell co-stimulatory signaling.  
– TLR and antigen processing pathways remain up in all myositis forms versus controls, but relative weighting shifts: innate IFN pathways dominate in DM, whereas adaptive checkpoints dominate in irMyositis.

Overall, GSEA reveals that irMyositis diverges from spontaneous DM by attenuating the classic IFN-driven antiviral signature and amplifying T-cell co-stimulatory circuits, consistent with an ICI-driven T-cell activation phenotype.
